title: Structural and functional characterization of the Streptococcus pneumoniae RrgB pilus backbone D1 domain.
experiment: 15N longitudinal (R1) and transverse (R2) relaxation and 15N{1H} NOE at 500 MHz (Lipari-Szabo model-free analysis with TENSOR2)
construct_or_mutation: recombinant C-terminal His-tagged RrgB N-terminal D1 domain (S. pneumoniae TIGR4)
other_conditions: protein concentration: 0.8 mM; tumbling: tau_c = 11.49 ± 1.9 ns (estimated from R2/R1 ratio); sequence-average R1 = 1.45 ± 0.1 s-1, R2 = 16.18 ± 1.5 s-1, 15N{1H} NOE = 0.71 ± 0.04; qualitative timescales stated in text: fast internal motions faster than tau_r (fitted tau_e in supplemental Fig. S2) and millisecond-microsecond conformational exchange (elevated R2 in supplemental Fig. S2)
related_structures: 2L40 (solution NMR structure of isolated RrgB D1 domain, 20 conformers, this work); 3HTL (C. diphtheriae SpaA N-terminal domain); 3KPT (B. cereus BcpA C-terminal CNA3 domain); 2PZ4 (S. agalactiae GBS52 N1 domain)
author_claim: 15N R1, R2, and 15N{1H} NOE measurements at 500 MHz (298 K, 0.8 mM) show homogeneous relaxation across the IgG-like beta-sandwich core of monomeric RrgB D1 (tau_c = 11.49 ± 1.9 ns), except at the N- and C-termini (including pilin-motif K183) and loops 56-69, 148-162, and 173-177: loops 56-69 and 148-162 display lower heteronuclear NOE and higher R1 from fast internal motions (fitted tau_e in supplemental Fig. S2), while regions 155-164 and 174-178 display elevated transverse R2 rates from millisecond-microsecond conformational exchange.
anchor: Heteronuclear relaxation measurements revealed that residues in the first two loops had heteronuclear NOE and longitudinal R1 values lower and higher than average, respectively (supplemental Fig. S2).
locator: Results, Solution Structure of the D1 Domain; Materials and Methods, Heteronuclear Relaxation Data; Discussion; supplemental Fig. S2
caveat_note: Deposit comparison (BMRB 17246, explicitly cited in footnote): temperature (298 K) and sheet field (500 MHz) match the card, but NMR buffer, pH, and exact recombinant D1 residue boundaries are in unavailable supplemental Materials and Methods / supplemental Tables S1 and S3 (card lists 20 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.2, 90% H2O/10% D2O, 175 aa); main text reports 0.8 mM protein concentration for 15N relaxation at 500 MHz, whereas BMRB 17246 lists S1 ([U-95% 15N], 0.5 mM), S2 (natural abundance, 0.9 mM), and S3 ([U-95% 13C; U-95% 15N], 0.4 mM), and bmrb_relaxation_field_MHz = 500/600 (main text lists 900, 800, 700, and 500 MHz spectrometers, never 600 MHz). Numeric fitted tau_e and per-residue R1/R2/NOE values are only in unavailable supplemental Fig. S2. Discussion also summarizes spatially proximal flexible regions near K183 as 49-69, 152-167, and 183-193.

title: Structural and functional characterization of the Streptococcus pneumoniae RrgB pilus backbone D1 domain.
experiment: 1H-15N HSQC and 3D triple-resonance backbone assignment spectra at 900, 800, 700, and 500 MHz
construct_or_mutation: recombinant C-terminal His-tagged RrgB N-terminal D1 domain (S. pneumoniae TIGR4)
other_conditions: 13C/15N-enriched, 15N-enriched, and unlabeled D1 samples (details in unavailable supplemental Materials and Methods and supplemental Table S3); beta9-beta10 loop (148-162) has backbone r.m.s.d. of about 2 Å in 2L40 ensemble (supplemental Fig. S1)
related_structures: 2L40 (solution NMR structure of isolated RrgB D1 domain, 20 conformers, this work); 3HTL (C. diphtheriae SpaA N-terminal domain); 3KPT (B. cereus BcpA C-terminal CNA3 domain); 2PZ4 (S. agalactiae GBS52 N1 domain)
author_claim: Backbone resonance assignments could not be obtained for eight residues (E143, H145, S146, S148, T149, Y150, V152, and G160) in and adjacent to the disordered beta9-beta10 loop, likely as a consequence of increased local mobility.
anchor: Thr-149, Tyr-150, Val-152, and Gly-160), likely as a consequence of an increased local mobility.
locator: Results, Solution Structure of the D1 Domain; conditions: Materials and Methods, NMR Characterization of RrgB D1 Domain
caveat_note: Chemical shifts from this study were deposited as BMRB 17246 at matching temperature (298 K), but NMR buffer, pH, and sample concentrations for assignment experiments are in unavailable supplemental Materials and Methods and supplemental Table S3 (card lists 20 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.2, 90% H2O/10% D2O, at 0.5 mM, 0.9 mM, and 0.4 mM). Unassigned amide resonances could reflect intermediate-timescale conformational exchange broadening and/or fast solvent exchange.
